result: h07. The avatar URL the browser loads is minted by the API converter (`AvatarUrl = "/file/" + userpb.Name + "/avatar"` → `/file/users/{username}/avatar`, `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:31-39`), rendered by `UserAvatar` (`web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx`) as a plain ``. That GET is served entirely outside gRPC, by the Echo file server: ``` GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar (route) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 RegisterRoutes (FileServerService) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121 (wired at server/server.go:80-81) serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 getCurrentUser → authenticator.AuthenticateToUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 (only when !Profile.AllowAnonymous()) getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148 Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:136 Driver.ListUsers (interface) — store/driver.go:47 DB.ListUsers (sqlite) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 | postgres: store/db/postgres/user.go:87 | mysql: store/db/mysql/user.go:84 SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? — store/db/sqlite/user.go:150-172 parseDataURI (decode base64 data URI) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:736 c.Blob (respond) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:209 ``` Details worth noting: - The `:identifier` path segment is treated strictly as a **username** — `getUserByUsername` builds `&store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}`; there's no ID fallback (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715-717`). - `Store.GetUser` consults `userCache` **only when `find.ID` is set**, so an avatar request always falls through to `ListUsers` → the driver → SQL; the row is written back into the cache afterwards (`store/user.go:148-169`). - The stored data is the `user.avatar_url` column itself, holding a `data:;base64,<...>` URI — not a file on disk. `parseDataURI` (regex at `fileserver.go:98`) splits it, and the MIME type is checked against `avatarAllowedTypes` before `c.Blob` writes the bytes with `nosniff` security headers and a long cache-control (`fileserver.go:196-209`). - Access control for *another* user's avatar: on a private instance (`!s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()`) any authenticated viewer suffices — session cookie, access token, or PAT via `authenticator.AuthenticateToUser`; there is no per-user check. On a public instance the endpoint is anonymous.
